title: 'Top Chef' Finalist Eric Adjepong Restricted to Supervised Visits With Daughter After Abuse Finding
excerpt: A Maryland judge issued a yearlong protective order against the celebrity chef after finding a preponderance of evidence that he physically abused his 7-year-old daughter.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Eric Adjepong faces a yearlong protective order limiting contact with his daughter after abuse findings.
  • The court found sufficient evidence of physical abuse against his 7-year-old daughter, Lennox.
  • Adjepong must complete parenting classes and therapy before unsupervised visits can resume.
  • DC police closed their investigation without charges, contradicting the civil court's findings.
  • Adjepong's ex-wife supports their daughter's claims, emphasizing the importance of her voice.

Celebrity chef Eric Adjepong, a finalist on Bravo's Top Chef: Kentucky and a regular on Food Network programming, has been barred from unsupervised contact with his 7-year-old daughter after a Maryland judge found sufficient evidence of physical abuse. The ruling, handed down on July 10 in Howard County Circuit Court, represents a dramatic turn for the 38-year-old chef whose culinary career has been built on a public persona of warmth and Ghanaian cultural pride.

What the Court Ordered

Judge Maurice C. Frazier determined there was a "preponderance of the evidence to believe" Adjepong physically abused his daughter, Lennox, according to court records reviewed by the Washington Post. The yearlong protective order, running through July 10, 2027, prohibits Adjepong from contacting, harassing, or threatening his daughter or his ex-wife Janelle Davis-Mack. Any visits with Lennox must be supervised.

https://x.com/theGrio/status/2080352533319459183

The order also mandates that Adjepong complete parenting classes and reunification therapy before any path to unsupervised contact can be considered.

Conflicting Findings Across Agencies

The case presents a striking split between criminal and civil proceedings. The District of Columbia Metropolitan Police Department closed its investigation without filing charges. The DC Child and Family Services Agency concluded its review with an "unfounded" disposition — which the agency defines as "not true."

Yet the Howard County Circuit Court, operating under the lower "preponderance of evidence" standard used in civil cases rather than the "beyond reasonable doubt" threshold required for criminal prosecution, reached the opposite conclusion.

The MPD confirmed to USA Today that its Youth Investigation Branch was notified of a sexual abuse allegation on May 1 by DC Child and Family Services. Detectives found no probable cause that a crime occurred and referred the case back to the agency.

Adjepong's Response

In a statement released through his attorney, Adjepong declined to address the specific allegations, citing his daughter's privacy.

"These allegations arose in the context of a long-running divorce and custody proceeding, which finally concluded on June 2, 2026."

— Eric Adjepong, via attorney statement

Adjepong said he has "the utmost respect for the Circuit Court" and is "strictly complying with every facet of the order." He expressed hope that he and his ex-wife could resolve matters "privately and through the proper legal channels, rather than in the press."

Davis-Mack wrote on Instagram on July 17 that her daughter "was brave enough to speak up against who should have been one of the most trusted adults in her life," adding: "I'll never stop believing her, protecting her, or reminding her that her voice matters."

Career Context

Adjepong rose to prominence as a finalist on Season 16 of Top Chef in 2018, where he became known for incorporating Ghanaian flavors and techniques into his cooking. He has since appeared on multiple Food Network series, including Guy Fieri's Tournament of Champions, Guy's Grocery Games, and Beat Bobby Flay. He operates a restaurant called Elmina.

Adjepong's Background

›Known for Ghanaian culinary techniques.

›Divorced in June 2026 after nearly five years.

The couple married after meeting at a house party in New York and separated in October 2021 after nearly five years of marriage. Davis-Mack filed for divorce in January 2022, and the proceedings were finalized on June 2, 2026. As part of the August 2024 divorce settlement, Adjepong was ordered to pay $804 per month in child support.

Food Network has not publicly commented on the protective order. The case remains an active civil matter in Howard County.
